report.narrative_markdown:
## Company overview

NVIDIA Corporation is a US-listed technology company in the semiconductors industry, with a market capitalization of $5.54T. It describes itself as a data center scale AI infrastructure company, serving customers in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe and other markets. It reports through two segments. Compute & Networking covers data center accelerated computing, networking platforms, AI solutions and software, and automotive platforms including autonomous and electric vehicle solutions. Graphics offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs, and Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics.

## Financial commentary

Revenue has risen sharply across the four fiscal years provided: $26.97B in 2023, $60.92B in 2024, $130.50B in 2025 and $215.94B in 2026. Net income followed the same path, from $4.37B in 2023 to $29.76B in 2024, $72.88B in 2025 and $120.07B in 2026. The input gives current revenue growth of 105.9% and a net margin of 63.7%, which shows profitability that is very high for a hardware business.

Returns and leverage also look strong. Return on equity is 117.2% and debt/equity is 0.17. The shares trade at $229.28, within a 52-week range of 164.27 to 243.37, close to the top of that range. The company recently announced a $150 billion increase to its share repurchase authorization, and the dividend yield is 0.4%.

## Comps commentary

The comparison uses forward P/E as the primary multiple, against a peer group of AMD, Broadcom, Intel, Marvell and Qualcomm. NVIDIA's forward P/E of 14.4 sits 62% below the peer median of 37.8. Its trailing P/E of 29.0 is 58% below the peer median of 68.2. On enterprise-value measures the discount is smaller: EV/EBITDA of 27.3 is 19% below the median of 33.7, and EV/Revenue of 18.2 is 8% below 19.8.

The operating comparisons run the other way. Net margin of 63.7% is 203% above the peer median of 21.0%, and revenue growth of 105.9% is 190% above the median of 36.5%. Debt/equity of 0.17 is 65% below the median of 0.49. In short, the company screens as cheaper than peers on earnings multiples while posting much stronger growth and profitability. Analyst sentiment in the data is a "strong_buy" consensus with a mean target of 328.72, but this report does not adopt it.
